name: Cube Computer

modes.label: Per-second VM sizes (50 GB disk)
modes.note: Per-size hour = calculator compute rate + mandatory 50 GB disk fee spread over 730 h (disk_month: $1.923 .. $7.488 per machine-month; compute_hour keeps the raw compute rate). The disk fee is charged for every month the machine exists, even when stopped, so bursty/short-lived use is under-counted by this hourly spread. Calculator prices embed a vendor subsidy (74% on 2 CPU/4 GB down to 0.2% on 16 CPU/128 GB): flagged promo (end date unpublished). 2 CPU 4 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 74.36% for this size; excludes mandatory $1.923/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 2 CPU 8 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 72.74% for this size; excludes mandatory $2.0445/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 4 CPU 8 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 69.33% for this size; excludes mandatory $2.30025/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 4 CPU 16 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 66.08% for this size; excludes mandatory $2.544/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 8 CPU 16 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 59.26% for this size; excludes mandatory $3.0555/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 16 CPU 32 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 39.12% for this size; excludes mandatory $4.566/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy. | 16 CPU 128 GB / 50 GB disk: Live calculator subsidy 0.16% for this size; excludes mandatory $7.488/machine-month disk. A different disk size changes compute and storage subsidy.

plans.name: Prepaid usage
plans.note: No subscription amount advertised in current calculator; hardware selection and prepaid credit. Starter-credit eligibility/amount unpublished. Access is through the Cube Mac app (GitHub sign-in); no public API and no published concurrency limit.

plans.name: Legacy subscription
plans.note: Existing subscribers only; monthly in advance at the price shown at checkout. They can switch to credits; active subscribers receive one month of their plan price as credit.

free.conditions: Eligible new accounts only; save a payment method. Claiming does not charge the card. The public page says the account shows the current offer and eligibility.

features.ip_note: Egress IPs and proxies not documented; terminal/SSH machine for coding agents with no managed browser.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

Rates are derived from public calculator implementation and verified by changing its controls in real Chrome. They are displayed calculator quotes, not a separately documented binding tariff. Raw unsubsidized costs must not be advertised as actual small-size retail prices.
Cube is a Linux cloud computer, not a cloud Mac: the macOS requirement refers to the client application. Fly.io hosts machines per privacy policy; dedicated CPU is vendor terminology.
All estimator modes pin disk to 50 GB. Storage charges are size-dependent, so card storage rate stays null; modes only estimate compute. Disk changes alter the subsidy on both compute and disk.

Public terms/privacy still mention subscriptions; current homepage says prepaid compute and disk. Starter credit amount, region, egress, free pause retention limits and billing increment are unverified. Privacy says machine contents retained until requested deletion, even when subscription lapses.

2026-09-28 (cube.computer): no public API / SDK: machines are created from the Mac app, so fleets (rl, ci) and API-driven presets cannot really use it; concurrency limits unpublished. Terminal / SSH cloud machine for coding agents: no desktop GUI or managed browser (desktop, browser set false).
Mandatory 50 GB disk now included in each size hour (disk_month / 730); billed monthly while the machine exists.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Pausing a prepaid Machine stops its running processes and compute charges. Persistent files remain, and storage continues to be charged.
snapshot_auto.note: Pause (manual, or automatic when prepaid credit runs out) keeps the persistent SSD only; running processes are stopped, no memory/state checkpoint. That is persistent_disk, not an automatic snapshot.

secret_proxy.quote: Your machine holds whatever you and your agents put there — source code, credentials,
secret_proxy.note: Agents use your own accounts; credentials are stored on the machine itself (the Backup download even includes 'saved credentials'). No proxy/injection feature.

isolation.quote: Application code runs in Firecracker microVMs. These are lightweight, secure virtual machines based on strong hardware virtualization.
isolation.note: derived: Cube's privacy policy names Fly.io as the operator of its cloud machines ('Fly.io — runs the cloud machines and stores their filesystems'); Fly.io's own docs confirm Firecracker microVMs. Cube itself does not name the hypervisor.

image_oci.quote: Debian — The operating system every Cube machine runs.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Machines are provisioned with a fixed Debian OS via the Mac app (sign in, pick repos, install agents); no custom Docker/OCI image start option is documented.

nested_virt.quote: Application code runs in Firecracker microVMs.
nested_virt.note: derived: Firecracker microVMs (the infrastructure Cube runs on, per its privacy policy) do not expose hardware virtualization / /dev/kvm to the guest; not documented by Cube itself.

computer_use.quote: Use the Mac app to start agents, run commands and check their progress.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cube is a terminal/SSH cloud machine for coding agents; no desktop GUI, browser, or screenshot+click API is offered.

anti_bot.quote: An always-on Linux cloud computer with a Mac app, for running coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No browser/scraping product surface exists to apply stealth/fingerprinting to.

captcha_solving.quote: An always-on Linux cloud computer with a Mac app, for running coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No browser automation or CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: Fly.io — runs the cloud machines and stores their filesystems.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: machines run on Fly.io cloud datacenter infrastructure; no residential/mobile/static IP product is documented.

snapshot.quote: Pausing a prepaid Machine stops its running processes and compute charges. Persistent files remain, and storage continues to be charged.
snapshot.note: Pause keeps the persistent disk only (no process/memory checkpoint). The app's 'Download files' Backup is a manual file export, not a disk or memory snapshot/restore mechanism, so no snapshot capability is documented.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Backup Backup contents Your files Download files Includes repos, worktrees, Git history, hidden files and saved credentials.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The only 'backup' feature is a manual file download from the Mac app; there is no API/CLI snapshot/checkpoint capability.

fork.quote: Parallel attempts | Fork the VM | A worktree per task
fork.note: Cube's own comparison page contrasts boat.dev's VM-fork feature with Cube's approach (a Git worktree per task on one machine), i.e. Cube has no fork capability.

fork_running.quote: Parallel attempts | Fork the VM | A worktree per task
fork_running.note: Depends on fork, which Cube does not offer.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Parallel attempts | Fork the VM | A worktree per task
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Depends on fork, which Cube does not offer.

pause_resume.quote: Paused | Persistent SSD storage. Compute stops; your files stay on the machine. ... Use Pause in the Machine tab to stop compute charges.

wake_on_request.quote: Adding credit doesn't start a paused machine. Use Start in the Machine tab when you're ready to run it.
wake_on_request.note: Starting a paused machine is a manual action in the app; no inbound request/traffic auto-wake is documented (Cube also has no documented inbound HTTPS feature).

volume_attach.quote: Your machine's CPU, memory, and SSD size determine its cost.
volume_attach.note: not offered: only a single built-in, resizable persistent SSD is documented; no separate attachable volume feature exists.

volume_shared.quote: A Cube is a computer in the cloud.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cube provisions one machine per user; there is no multi-machine shared-volume feature.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Closing the app does not pause a Machine or stop its charges.
auto_stop_idle.note: The machine only pauses when prepaid credit is exhausted or the user manually pauses it; there is no idle-activity-based auto-stop documented.

live_resize.quote: Use Edit specs in the Machine tab to adjust CPU, memory, and storage. Review the quoted cost and any restart or file-copy confirmation before applying a change.
live_resize.note: Resizing can require a restart/file-copy confirmation, so it is not documented as a seamless live resize of a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: Install command-line agents on your Cube and run them against your repositories. ... Claude Code Codex CLI OpenCode Hermes Agent OpenClaw Pi fx Gemini CLI Aider goose Amp Cursor CLI GitHub Copilot CLI Droid Crush Qwen Code Kimi Code CLI Mistral Vibe Continue CLI Kiro CLI

harness_api.note: No public API/SDK is published; the site only advertises the Mac app, SSH, and manual agent installs from a list (per card caveat: 'no public API / SDK').

own_agent_api.quote: Install command-line agents on your Cube and run them against your repositories.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cube runs third-party coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.); it has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: An always-on cloud computer for Claude Code & Codex
mcp_server.note: No MCP server for controlling Cube sandboxes is mentioned anywhere on the site, guides, or GitHub org.

lang_node.quote: Install command-line agents on your Cube and run them against your repositories. Claude Code Codex CLI OpenCode ...
lang_node.note: derived: the listed coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, etc.) are npm-distributed Node.js tools that Cube installs and runs on the machine, implying Node.js is available; not separately confirmed as a standalone runtime claim.

public_ipv4.note: Not documented. SSH access is configured by the Mac app ('Allow SSH from this Mac'), suggesting app-managed/keyed access rather than an advertised public IPv4 per machine; no public IPv4 feature is mentioned.

inbound_https.quote: An always-on Linux cloud computer with a Mac app, for running coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cube is built for running coding-agent sessions, not for hosting/exposing web services; no HTTPS ingress feature is documented.

ingress_rules.quote: An always-on Linux cloud computer with a Mac app, for running coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, since there is no documented inbound HTTPS/port-exposure feature to control access to.

egress_allowlist.quote: Security Traffic is encrypted in transit. Access to production systems is limited to people who need it.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented; the security section covers only transit encryption and internal access control.

egress_http_rules.quote: Security Traffic is encrypted in transit. Access to production systems is limited to people who need it.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no method/path-level egress rules are documented.

guest_firewall.note: derived: Cube is a full Debian VM with root/SSH access (root=true per card), so nftables/iptables should work inside; not separately documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Fly.io — runs the cloud machines and stores their filesystems.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented; card's own ip_note says egress IPs and proxies are not documented.

gpu.quote: Your machine's CPU, memory, and SSD size determine its cost.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Machine sizing is CPU/RAM/disk only; no GPU option is listed anywhere on the site.

self_host.quote: Cube Computer provides cloud machines for running coding agents, together with a desktop application for working with them.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cube is a hosted SaaS product; there is no self-hosted deployment option.

byoc.quote: Fly.io — runs the cloud machines and stores their filesystems.
byoc.note: not offered: machines run on Fly.io infrastructure operated by Cube; no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment is documented.

open_source.quote: Desktop release feed for Cube Computer — published by the release pipeline, do not edit directly
open_source.note: The public collabs-inc GitHub repos are a release/update feed and an unrelated legacy product, not the Cube application source; the licenses page only credits third-party OSS dependencies used inside a closed-source product.

soc2.quote: Security Traffic is encrypted in transit. Access to production systems is limited to people who need it. No system is perfectly secure, and we do not claim otherwise.
soc2.note: not offered: no compliance/trust page or SOC 2 attestation is mentioned anywhere on the site.

hipaa.quote: Security Traffic is encrypted in transit. Access to production systems is limited to people who need it.
hipaa.note: not offered: no HIPAA/BAA program is mentioned anywhere on the site; small consumer-oriented product.

sso.quote: Account data. When you sign in through GitHub we receive your username, email address, and the account identifier.
sso.note: The only documented authentication method is GitHub OAuth sign-in; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO is offered.

eu_data_residency.quote: These providers operate in the United States and elsewhere. Where data leaves the UK or the European Economic Area we rely on the transfer mechanisms available to us, including standard contractual clauses.
eu_data_residency.note: The privacy policy discusses transferring EU/UK data out under SCCs rather than offering a choice to keep machines/data in EU regions; no region-selection or residency guarantee is documented.

max_session_h.quote: Session length | Up to 24 hours (1 hour default) | Always on
max_session_h.note: Cube's own comparison page states its machines are 'Always on' (contrasted with the 24h-limited competitor), i.e. no maximum session length; the machine runs until paused/stopped by the user or credit runs out.

docker_inside.quote: Debian — The operating system every Cube machine runs.
docker_inside.note: derived: Cube is a full Debian Linux VM (card isolation="vm") reached over root SSH ("ssh cube") with persistent disk and no listed OS/package restrictions; running Docker on such a machine needs only the guest kernel's own namespaces/overlayfs, not nested virtualization. Not separately documented as a named feature by Cube.

arm64.quote: Your machine’s CPU, memory, and SSD size determine its cost. ... Use Edit specs in the Machine tab to adjust CPU, memory, and storage.
arm64.note: not offered: the pricing/spec picker only lets you choose vCPU count, memory and disk size — there is no architecture option, and no Cube page mentions ARM/aarch64 machines. Machines run on Fly.io per the privacy policy, whose default fleet Cube uses without any ARM selection.

desktop.quote: Cube is an always-on Linux computer in the cloud, with a Mac app, for running coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. ... Connect over SSH (`ssh cube`) from any terminal or editor
desktop.note: Cube is a headless Linux machine reached via SSH/terminal from a macOS client app; there is no remote desktop GUI on the machine itself.

browser.quote: A full Linux computer in the cloud, driven from a dedicated Mac app. ... Connect over SSH (`ssh cube`) from any terminal or editor; Cube sets up the keys and config.
browser.note: Product is a terminal/SSH machine for running coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, etc.); no managed/embedded browser or browser-automation feature is offered or documented.

windows.quote: Cube is an always-on Linux computer in the cloud, with a Mac app
windows.note: The cloud machine itself is Linux-only; no Windows machine option exists anywhere on the site.

macos.quote: The Cube app runs on macOS only.
macos.note: macOS refers only to the client/controller app; the cloud computer being controlled is Linux, not a cloud Mac machine.
